etymarab.kok_maddesi: Back to library EtymArab ḪṬː (ḪṬṬ) خطّ/خطط BP – • HDAL • © SG | 15Mar2023, last update 17Jan2026 √ ḪṬː (ḪṬṬ) “root” ▪ ḪṬː (ḪṬṬ)_1 ‘to draw or trace a line; to draw, sketch, design; to write, pen; to carve, engrave, inscribe’ ↗ ḫaṭṭa ; ‘line, stroke, stripe; (railroad, telephone) line, airline, frontline; handwriting, calligraphy; furrow, ridge’ ↗ ḫaṭṭ ; ‘full section, district, quarter (of a city) ↗ ḫuṭṭ ; ‘piece of land, of real estate, lot; district; map, plan; project, design, intention; policy, rule, guiding principle’ ↗ ḫiṭṭaẗ ~ ḫuṭṭaẗ ; ‘manuscript’ ↗ maḫṭūṭaẗ ▪ ḪṬː (ḪṬṬ)_2 ‘…’ ↗ … ♦ Semantic value spectrum in ClassAr (acc. to BAH2008): ‘furrows, roads; lines, pen markings, writing, stripes; living quarters; affair, plan, intention; to write’ ▪ [gnrl] : It seems that there is only one main value attached to this root: [v1]; derivations are easily discernable (for details, see ↗ ḫaṭṭ and ↗ ḫaṭṭa ). ▪ [v1] : According to Kogan2015: 335-6 (#14, fn 988), Ar ḫaṭṭ ‘line, streak, stripe’ »in all likelihood represents an internal Ar derivation from the verbal root ḫṭṭ ‘to make a mark upon the ground’, further related to Akk ḫaṭāṭu ‘to make a ditch, excavate’, Syr ḥaṭ ‘effodit’, JBA ḥṭṭ ‘to dig out’ and, possibly, Tña ḥaṭäṭ bälä ‘to scratch’. – The same author thinks that Akk ḫaṭṭu ‘scepter, staff, stick, branch, twig’ and Ug ḫṭ ‘sceptre, rod, wand, stake’ (widely attested) (Akk-Ug * ḫaṭṭ - ‘rod’) are no reliable cognates. For the same reason, probably, also DRS treats the Akk-Ug items separately (as #ḪṬṬ-1). ▪ [v1] : On account of Akk and modSAr cognates (but Ar not taken into consideration!), StarLing (#1686) reconstructs Sem * ḫVṭ- ‘to dig; to make signs on the ground’. Taken together with the hypothetical forms in ECh (* gatt- ḫVṭ- ), LEC (* haḍ- ) and HEC (* haḍ- ), all signifying ‘to dig’, the authors go yet a step further and posit AfrAs * Haṭ- ‘to dig’. ▪ … – ▪ DRS 10 (2012) #ḪṬṬ- 1 […]. - 2 Akk ḫaṭāṭu ‘creuser, excaver; draguer (une rivière)’, ‘faire une incision’, nHbr ḥāṭaṭ , Syr ḥaṭ ‘creuser’, Ar ḫaṭṭa ‘tracer des lignes sur le sol’, ḫiṭṭaẗ : terrain marqué d’un signe pour montrer qu’on peut y bâtir, ḫaṭṭāṭ ‘calligraphe, géomancien’, EAr ḫaṭṭ ‘écrire une lettre ensorcelée’, ḫaṭwaṭ ‘faire des sillons’, Sab ḫṭṭ ‘délimiter (des terres à coloniser)’, ḫṭ ‘écrire’, ḫṭṭ ‘ensorcellement’, Mhr ḫəṭ , Jib ḫeṭṭ ‘écrire, tracer des signes sur le sol pour indiquer une route’, Ḥrs ḫṭāṭ ‘tracer des signes sur le sol pour indiquer une route’. – Outside Sem: (Cush) Dahalo ḥuḍ ‘creuser’ (so OrelStolbova_ HSED ). – - 3 - 5 […]. ▪ Kogan2015: 335-6 (#14, fn 988): Akk ḫaṭāṭu ‘to make a ditch, excavate’, Syr ḥaṭ ‘effodit’, JBA ḥṭṭ ‘to dig out’, Ar ḫaṭṭ ‘to make a mark upon the ground’, ḫaṭṭ ‘line, streak, stripe’, possibly also Tña ḥaṭäṭ bälä ‘to scratch’. ▪ StarLing: Akk ḫaṭāṭu ‘to dig’, Mhr ḫeṭ , Ḥrs ḫtat ‘to make signs on the ground’. [No Ar cognates mentioned!] – Outside Sem: (ECh) Birgit gàttí , (LEC) Or (Galla) haaḍa , (HEC) Dahalo, Dahalo (Sanye) ḥuḍ- ‘to dig’. ▪ See above, section CONC. – – Sources ; meta ; gram ; engl ; conc ; hist ; cogn ; disc ; west ; deriv ;
